Not really but it's more easy to do with the export. It's avoid something like:

```js
shallow(<Enhance {...props} />)
    .find('Slider-HeaderFooter')
    .shallow()
    .find('Slider')
    .shallow()
    .find('Rheostat')
```

It's not a breaking change, just a fix in the documentation.

- The `refine` function is already called with [an array and not an object](https://github.com/algolia/instantsearch.js/pull/2408/files#diff-6594f5647a134a790a0668875d7b1045L131).
- The property `numeric` doesn't exist on the render function, [it's name is `range`](https://github.com/algolia/instantsearch.js/pull/2408/files#diff-6594f5647a134a790a0668875d7b1045L210).

body:
I tried to kept the compatibility.

In the previous version the range was compute with the stats object in the [init](https://github.com/algolia/instantsearch.js/blob/develop/src/connectors/range-slider/connectRangeSlider.js#L169) and the [render](https://github.com/algolia/instantsearch.js/blob/develop/src/connectors/range-slider/connectRangeSlider.js#L194) functions. Then thoses values are rounded when passed to the rendering function. But it might happen that the stats object can be `{ min: null, max: null }` and `null` is rounded to `0`.

The `0` case is used in `RangeSlider` for [hide it](https://github.com/algolia/instantsearch.js/blob/develop/src/widgets/range-slider/range-slider.js#L44) when there are nothing to display. In upcoming version we can imagine to pass a `disabled` property instead of rely on range values.
